The story achieves a very effective balance between scene and summary/exposition. The primary narrative unfolds in real-time as a vivid scene at the ferry dock, utilizing dialogue, physical actions (checking the rope, the suitcase wheel getting stuck), and sensory details to create tension between Ilse and her son, Jonas. 

Woven seamlessly into this scene are brief, well-placed moments of summary and exposition. For example, the third paragraph summarizes Ilse's actions just prior to docking to establish her emotional avoidance, while small expositional details—such as the mention of Henning painting the shutters the previous spring and Jonas’s resemblance to his father—provide crucial backstory about a recent family loss without halting the momentum of the present-day interaction.
